messages:
Jordan Lee: Quick design check — uploaded a small tweak to the capacity card: moved the burst toggle next to the pool picker and added an illustrative microchart to show effective throughput. can people skim? :eyes:
Aisha Patel: skimmed. visual feels clearer but the burst toggle now competes with the GPU pool dropdown for visual weight. maybe reduce the toggle prominence or move it under an overflow?
Marcus Chen: Agree on weight. Also keyboard users will tab into the dropdown then the toggle — that might be surprising. We should define the focus order: pool -> min -> max -> burst -> sla slider. Is that intentional?
Jordan Lee: Intended to keep burst after cap controls because burst affects peak not baseline. But we can change. What do folks think about grouping min/max together with a shared label and making burst a separate cluster?
Priya Singh: Grouping min/max visually and with aria grouping is good. For screen readers: add "aria-describedby" on the group that says "baseline capacity (min to max)". And ensure the burst toggle has aria-pressed and a visible focus ring.
Aisha Patel: Copy nits: current copy under burst says "Enable burst capacity for short periods." Suggest: "Enable short bursts of extra capacity — billed only when used." shorter: "Short bursts of extra capacity (billed when used)"
Marcus Chen: +1 on copy tweak. Also from a keyboard/a11y standpoint, when burst is toggled on we show a numeric field for 'burst cap'. That field should be focusable immediately after the toggle, not skipped. Add focus-trap or programmatic focus in the toggle's change handler.
Jordan Lee: Good call. Prototype change: on enable, focus moves to burst cap. On disable, focus returns to max. Any objections?
Priya Singh: Works. For the visual microchart, contrast is low on the orange fill at small sizes. Need at least 4.5:1 against background. If we can't hit that, add a 1px dark outline to the shape or use a different pattern.
figma-bot: New frame uploaded: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/capacity-controls?node-id=142%3A8 — see frames "compact-variant" and "a11y-focus"
Aisha Patel: One more: keyboard users expect stepper controls to respond to up/down arrow for single increments. Make sure our custom steppers listen to arrow keys, not just the +/- buttons. Also add aria-label like "Minimum GPUs" / "Maximum GPUs".
Marcus Chen: Technical note: current react component uses onChange that only updates on blur for steppers. For immediate arrow response we need to call setState on keydown. I'll follow up with a small PR.
Jordan Lee: Thanks. Last quick ask — can we surface an inline guardrail hint when min > max? Right now validation shows up as a modal error. Prefer inline text: "Min cannot exceed Max" in red under the steppers.
Priya Singh: +1. Inline validation is both better for keyboard users and screen readers if we update aria-invalid and aria-errormessage pointing to the text.
Aisha Patel: UX copy for guardrail: "Min cannot exceed Max — reduce Min or increase Max." keep it simple.
Jordan Lee: Ok will update prototype with: grouping, copy tweaks, focus behavior (on enable move to burst cap), inline validation, contrast fix. I'll post a short screenshot when done. Thanks all :rocket:
figma-bot: Comment added on frame "a11y-focus" by Jordan Lee: "Set focus to burst cap when enabled; aria-live for validation"
Jordan Lee: Screenshot: https://img.redwood.ai/snap/1768124590-compact-capacity.png
Aisha Patel: Looks much better. thumbs up :thumbsup:
Marcus Chen: I'll open the PR for the keydown behavior tomorrow.
Priya Singh: I'll write the a11y test notes for QA and link them in the ticket.
Jordan Lee: Filing the follow-up ticket now and tagging y'all. Thanks!
